land.text: the remnant realm of the Malacca sultans after 1511 (Bintan, Kampar), which Alauddin Riayat Shah II rebuilt on the Johor River; the infobox lists the Malacca Sultanate as predecessor

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps a 'Sultanate of Malacca' row to 1861 that overlaps the Johor years; the se-02 Malacca dossier must settle it.

land.text: Pahang, a separate sultanate (est. 1470) until it entered a nominal dynastic union with Johor in 1623; the Johor infobox lists the Pahang Sultanate as a predecessor

predecessors.note: Joined 1623, not at birth; the 1528 shape in this dossier therefore excludes Pahang. The Pahang Sultanate 1470-1623 has no Cliopatria row: pahang-sultanate (1853-1889) is a different era.

land.text: the whole of Cliopatria's last Johor shape (mainland Johor); the 1885 British Colonial Empire shape contains all 61 cells of it

successors.note: The pages opened are silent on why Cliopatria ends the row in 1884; see notes.
Earlier partial break-away, not the end-of-life handover.

land.text: Riau and Lingga, the Dutch half of the 1824 partition
Pahang, treated as separate from Johor by the 1861 treaty

successors.note: Earlier partial break-away (1861); Cliopatria draws it from 1853.

capitals.name: Pekan Tua (Johor River)
capitals.note: Infobox lists Sayong Pinang from the 1530s; the text says the sultanate was 'based at Pekan Tua'. Coordinates approximate (+-15 km); none of the seats is in the gazetteer.

capitals.note: Infobox 1564-1570, after the Acehnese sack of Johor Lama. Coordinates approximate.

capitals.name: Batu Sawar (Kota Tinggi)
capitals.note: Infobox 1587-1618, after the Portuguese sack of Johor Lama. Coordinates approximate.

capitals.name: Lingga
capitals.note: Infobox 1618-1625; Raja Bujang had fled to Lingga in 1617 (Pahang Sultanate page). The infobox then gives 'no fixed place' 1625-1640.

capitals.name: Batu Sawar (Kota Tinggi)
capitals.note: Infobox 1640-1675; sacked by Jambi in 1673. The infobox gives 'no fixed place' 1675-1688 (court in Pahang, then Riau).

capitals.name: Pancur
capitals.note: Infobox 1700-1708 and 1715-1720; site not placed on any page, coordinates a guess near the Johor River.

capitals.name: Riau (Bintan)
capitals.note: Infobox 1708-1715; Tanjungpinang is in the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Riau (Bintan)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Riau: 1720 onward', end year not given; 'Sultan Abdul Rahman was installed as the Sultan of Lingga in November 1822'. After the 1824 partition the pages opened give no seat for the mainland state.

rulers.name: Alauddin Riayat Shah II
rulers.note: Sultans table of the Johor Sultanate page.

rulers.name: Ali Jalla Abdul Jalil Shah II
Mahmud Shah II
rulers.note: 'the sultan was assassinated in 1699'; last of the Malacca dynasty.

rulers.name: Abdul Jalil Rahmat Shah (Raja Kecil)
rulers.title: rival sultan
rulers.note: Overlaps Abdul Jalil IV; 'In 1722, Raja Kecil was dethroned by Raja Sulaiman's supporters'.

rulers.name: Abdul Rahman Muazzam Shah
rulers.note: The infobox gives 1811-1819 and the body text says he died in 1832; the table says 1812-1830. List stops here: the page has no ruler list for the mainland line after 1830.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1529 shape without Pahang (a separate sultanate until 1623) and the Jambi lowlands: southern Johor, Terengganu, the Riau Islands, the Sumatran shore (Riau) and Singapore

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the sultanate was 'founded in 1528' but Cliopatria begins in 1529. Same corrected shape as 1529 (Pahang and the Jambi lowlands removed). Cliopatria area 208,008 km2 against the infobox 220,000 km2 (no year given): ratio 0.95, fine.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1529 shape minus Pahang and minus the Jambi lowlands

keyframe_review.note: Pahang is wrong in 1529-1622: the Pahang page has it as an independent sultanate from 1470 (a Malacca vassal until 1511) that 'entered a nominal dynastic union with Johor in 1623', and Johor's army only 'overran the suburbs of Pekan' in September 1612. The 100 Jambi cells are wrong too: the Jambi page has a Jambi kingdom since 1460 and a Mataram vassal until 1663/64 (Cliopatria's Jambi row only starts 1670 and covers the same cells). Applies 1529-1608.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1609 shape minus Pahang and minus the Jambi lowlands, for 1609-1622

keyframe_review.note: Same correction as 1529 for 1609-1622 (Pahang separate until the 1623 union, Jambi independent of Johor); the shape is cell-for-cell the 1529 shape. From 1623 see sultanate-of-johor_1623.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1609 shape (Pahang included) minus the Jambi lowlands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1623-1625: Pahang joins in 1623 ('a nominal dynastic union with Johor in 1623, when Johor's Abdullah Ma'ayat Shah died'); the Jambi lowlands stay out.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1626 shape minus the Jambi lowlands

keyframe_review.note: Pahang stays (union 1623); the Jambi lowlands stay out until Johor's 1655 gain of Tungkal and the Johor-Jambi war. The shape loses 3 cells in north Sumatra against 1609 (Cliopatria's Aceh row, 1626-1639, overlaps the 1529 shape in exactly 3 cells): small, and the pages opened do not date it (J: 'Aceh suffered a defeat at the Battle of Duyon River' 1629), so it is left as drawn. Applies 1626-1669.

The 1670 shape (573 cells) equals the 1626 shape minus the Jambi lowlands, so this is the shape the corrections above converge on; the 'loss' in Cliopatria in 1670 is only the start of Cliopatria's Jambi row, not a Johor event (the war with Jambi, 1667-1679, left Johor's borders unchanged). Applies 1670-1690.

correction.text: shape unchanged; the years change: 1691-1721 (the Terengganu cells leave in 1722, not 1727)

keyframe_review.note: Cell-for-cell the 1670 shape; applies 1691-1721 only. Terengganu emerged as an independent sultanate in 1722, five years before Cliopatria drops it.

Right shape (no Terengganu), wrong start: 'Terengganu emerged as an independent sultanate in 1722 with the installation of the first sultan, Zainal Abidin I', so this shape applies from 1722 to 1819. The Terengganu page adds that 'In 1741, Sultan Sulaiman of Johor appointed Sultan Mansur as the ruler of Terengganu', a sign of residual Johor authority.

correction.text: the 1727-1819 shape (mainland Johor, Pahang, Riau Islands, Sumatran shore) held to 1823

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1820-1823: Cliopatria drops the Sumatran shore and the Riau Islands in 1820, but the Johor page puts the partition at the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 ('Sultan Abdul Rahman was installed as the Sultan of Lingga in November 1822', 'ruled under the auspices of the Dutch'). Cliopatria's Riau-Lingga row also starts 1820; that dossier (se-03) should check 1820 against 1824.

Right shape, wrong start: the partition is the Anglo-Dutch Treaty signed 17 March 1824 (transfers due 1 March 1825). Cliopatria's 62,290 km2 shape (mainland Johor, Pahang, part of Kelantan, four islands) applies 1824-1860, see 1853. The 13 Kelantan cells and the Pahang cells are not argued by any page opened.

The Johor page has the 1861 treaty between Temenggong Daeng Ibrahim and Bendahara Tun Mutahir recognising 'Johor and Pahang as separate' independent states; Pahang is described as one of four Bendahara fiefs before that. Cliopatria separates them in 1853 (its Pahang Sultanate row starts 1853). The Johor shape of 61 cells applies from 1861; 1853-1860 stays on the 1820 shape. Flag for the Pahang dossier (se-03).

Cell-for-cell the 1853 shape (19,546 km2); mainland Johor as Newbold described it in 1836: 'Muar, Batu Pahat, Pontian, Sedili and Johor Lama'. Applies 1880-1884; nothing on the pages opened explains why Cliopatria ends the row in 1884.

region.text: the new capital by the Johor River (Pekan Tua), with the Riau Islands, Singapore and the southern Malay Peninsula that Malacca had held

ledger.note: 1528: Alauddin Riayat Shah II founds the Johor Sultanate at Pekan Tua. 'Foundation of the Sultanate: 1528'; 'founded in 1528 by Sultan' Alauddin and 'based at Pekan Tua'; the territory was 'most of Malacca's former territory including the southern Malay Peninsula', plus parts of southeastern Sumatra and the Riau Islands. The page names the places, not a boundary; Cliopatria starts one year later (1529).

region.text: parts of southeastern Sumatra (Kampar, Siak, Bengkalis) and the Terengganu coast

ledger.note: 1528: the Sumatran shore and Terengganu come with the inheritance of Malacca. The page lists Kampar, Siak, Bengkalis and Terengganu only 'at its height' without a year, and says the sultan 'retreated to Kampar in Sumatra' after the Portuguese razed Bintan in 1526; the date here is a bridging reading of Cliopatria's 1529 shape.
1564: the Acehnese sack Johor Lama and the court moves to Bukit Seluyut. 'was sacked by the Acehnese in 1564'; infobox Bukit Seluyut 1564-1570.
1570: the court returns to Johor Lama (infobox 'Johor Lama: 1536-1564 and 1570-1587').
1587: the Portuguese sack Johor Lama and the capital moves to Batu Sawar. 'attacked and sacked by the Portuguese' in 1587; infobox Batu Sawar 1587-1618.

region.text: Pekan and its suburbs, the Pahang capital

ledger.note: 1612: a Johor army attacks Pekan, Pahang's capital. 'In September 1612, the Johor army overran the suburbs of Pekan' (Pahang page); Pahang is an independent sultanate until the 1623 union.

region.text: Pekan and its suburbs, the Pahang capital

ledger.note: 1613: Pahang beats Johor with Brunei's help and keeps its independence until the 1623 union (Pahang page: Pahang defeated Johor in 1613 with Brunei's help; the page gives no month for the battle). The Johor page notes Aceh attacking Johor itself 'in 1613 and again in 1615'.
1618: the court moves to Lingga (infobox Lingga 1618-1625); the Pahang page has Raja Bujang fleeing to Lingga in 1617 before the Acehnese.

region.text: Pahang, in a nominal dynastic union with Johor

ledger.note: 1623: Pahang and Johor share one ruler. 'Pahang entered a nominal dynastic union with Johor in 1623, when Johor's Abdullah Ma'ayat Shah died' and Raja Bujang became ruler of both as Abdul Jalil Shah III. A personal union, drawn as Johor land because Cliopatria and the Johor infobox ('Predecessors: Pahang Sultanate') do.
1640: the court returns to Batu Sawar (infobox Batu Sawar 1640-1675, 'no fixed place' 1625-1640).

region.text: Tungkal, on the Jambi coast, 'under Jambian sovereignty until a pro-Johorese rebellion forced them out in 1655'

ledger.note: 1655: Tungkal rebels against Jambi and passes to Johor. 'Tungkal remained under Jambian sovereignty until a pro-Johorese rebellion forced them out in 1655' (Jambi page); the page does not say Johor annexed it, and Tungkal is not in the gazetteer (a 60 km radius is drawn).

region.text: the mouth of the Jambi River, Tungkal and Indragiri

ledger.note: 1667: the war with Jambi opens at sea. 'In May 1667, a Johorese fleet destroyed the fishing huts and orchards at the mouth of the Jambi River'; 'In August 1670, Jambian forces raided Indragiri and Tungkal, taking 917 slaves'; the Johor page says the war began in 1666.

1675: with Batu Sawar sacked by Jambi, the court has no fixed seat until 1688. Johor page: 'its capital, Batu Sawar, was sacked by Jambi in 1673' (Jambi page: 'On April 4, 1673'); infobox 'No fixed place: 1675-1688', the court in Pahang 1675-1680, then Riau 1680-1688 (text and infobox differ slightly).

region.text: the mouth of the Jambi River, Tungkal and Indragiri

ledger.note: 1679: Johor wins the war with Jambi, no border moves. 'In May 1679, the Johorese launched an attack on Jambi with 300 ships'; 'On October 17, 1679, Daeng Mangika fled to Palembang'; the Johor page: 'Johor won in 1679, but the Bugis stayed on'.
1688: the court settles at Kota Tinggi (infobox Kota Tinggi 1688-1700).

1699: Sultan Mahmud II is assassinated and the Bendahara dynasty takes the throne. 'the sultan was assassinated in 1699' by Megat Sri Rama; Mahmud II left no heirs; the table lists 'Abdul Jalil IV (Bendahara dynasty): 1699-1720'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).
1700: the capital moves to Pancur (infobox Pancur 1700-1708 and 1715-1720).
1708: the capital moves to Riau (infobox Riau 1708-1715).
1715: the capital returns to Pancur (infobox 1715-1720).
1720: the capital returns to Riau (infobox 'Riau: 1708-1715 and 1720 onward').

region.text: Terengganu, which 'emerged as an independent sultanate'

ledger.note: 1722: Terengganu becomes an independent sultanate. 'Terengganu emerged as an independent sultanate in 1722 with the installation of the first sultan, Zainal Abidin I'; 'In 1741, Sultan Sulaiman of Johor appointed Sultan Mansur as the ruler of Terengganu'. Cliopatria draws the loss in 1727. The Johor page says Terengganu was part of the sultanate 'at its height' only. The same year 'Raja Kecil was dethroned by Raja Sulaiman's supporters' with Bugis help.

region.text: Singapore, where Raffles landed on 29 January 1819, 'nominally ruled by Johor'

ledger.note: 1819: the British take a trading post at Singapore. Raffles's expedition arrived in Singapore on 29 January 1819; Hussein and the Temenggong receive 'a yearly stipend from the British'; 'This treaty was ratified on 6 February 1819'. The page speaks of a trading post, not a cession of sovereignty; Cliopatria's 1820 shape no longer includes Singapore.

region.text: Riau and Lingga: the Anglo-Dutch Treaty 'split the Sultanate of Johor into modern Johor and the Riau-Lingga Sultanate'

ledger.note: 1824: the Anglo-Dutch Treaty splits the Johor-Riau empire. Johor page: the treaty 'split the Sultanate of Johor into modern Johor and the Riau-Lingga Sultanate', signed without the knowledge of the sultan. Anglo-Dutch Treaty page: signed in London on 17 March 1824, ratified 30 April and 2 June 1824, transfers due 1 March 1825; the British agree not to make treaties with rulers on islands 'south of the strait of Singapore'. Cliopatria cuts in 1820; the Sultan was installed at Lingga in November 1822. Reviewer se-02-f: confidence lowered from 3 to 2. The Johor page names only the insular part as going to the Dutch ('the mainland part was administered by the British, and the insular part by the Dutch'); the Sumatran shore (the Riau admin1 in this region) is not named for 1824, and the infobox lists the Siak Sultanate among Johor's successors.

1855: Tengku Ali gives up Johor to Temenggong Ibrahim. The 1855 treaty between Temenggong Ibrahim and Tengku Ali required Tengku Ali to 'give up all of Johor' in exchange for recognition as sultan; the mainland state continues under the Temenggong line (same colour). The page does not mention Muar, Sultan Abu Bakar or any 1885 treaty.

region.text: Pahang, recognised as a separate state under the Bendahara

ledger.note: 1861: Johor and Pahang are recognised as separate states. Temenggong Daeng Ibrahim signed a treaty with Bendahara Tun Mutahir of Pahang recognising the two as separate; 'the remnants of the empire became two independent states, Johor and Pahang'. Cliopatria draws the separation in 1853 (its Pahang Sultanate row starts 1853).

region.text: Cliopatria's last Johor shape, mainland Johor

ledger.note: 1884: Cliopatria's Johor row ends and its British Colonial Empire shape covers all of Johor from 1885. The pages opened give no event for 1884 or 1885 (no Abu Bakar, no treaty); the page's infobox lists 'Johor Sultanate (modern)' among the successors. Page silent: a gap-filler should open the page on Abu Bakar of Johor or the History of Johor.

wars.name: Acehnese and Portuguese attacks on Johor
wars.outcome: Johor Lama sacked by Aceh (1564) and by the Portuguese (1587); Aceh attacked again in 1613 and 1615. The capital moved each time; no land changed hands.
wars.note: 'Johor Lama was sacked by the Acehnese in 1564'; 'attacked and sacked by the Portuguese' in 1587; 'Aceh attacked Johor in 1613 and again in 1615'. No separate war article opened.

wars.name: Johor-Pahang war
wars.outcome: Pahang repelled Johor in 1613, with Brunei's help, and stayed independent until the 1623 union.
wars.note: The Pahang page gives September 1612 for the attack on Pekan and 1613 for the Pahang victory.

wars.name: Dutch-Portuguese War: siege of Malacca

zones.text: Malacca, which Johor and the Dutch 'conquered on January 14, 1641'

wars.outcome: Malacca passed to the Dutch East India Company; the Dutch 'agreed not to seek territories or wage war against Johor'. Johor gained no land.
wars.note: The page gives January 14, 1641 for the fall; the start of the siege is not given.

wars.name: Johor-Jambi war

zones.text: the Jambi River mouth, Tungkal and Indragiri

wars.outcome: Jambi sacked Batu Sawar on 4 April 1673 and Johor won the war in 1679 (Daeng Mangika fled to Palembang on 17 October 1679); no border moved.
wars.note: No Wikipedia article 'Johor-Jambi War' was found; the story is in the Jambi Sultanate page. The Johor page dates the war 1666-1679 ('The war began in 1666').

wars.name: Raja Kecil's usurpation
wars.outcome: Raja Kecil of Siak held the Johor throne until 'dethroned by Raja Sulaiman's supporters' with Bugis help in 1722; the Bugis then dominated the sultanate 1760-1784. No border moved.
wars.note: The page gives no year of 1717 and the infobox dates the rebellion to 1718. The Siak Sultanate has no dossier.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line; the Sumatran shore and the Peninsula coast are approximate.

The Singapore Strait line of the 1824 treaty is a treaty line (sharp) between Johor and the Dutch sphere, but only as a sea line; the land frontiers with Pahang (1861 treaty) and Malacca are not surveyed.

notes:
Five pages opened (budget 5). The Wikipedia article 'Johor-Jambi War' returned URL_NOT_FOUND (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johor%E2%80%93Jambi_War); the Jambi Sultanate page replaced it.
CLIOPATRIA ERRORS CORRECTED: (1) Pahang is inside the 1529-1622 shapes but was a separate sultanate until the 1623 union; (2) 100 cells of Jambi province are inside the 1529-1669 shapes although Jambi was an independent kingdom (Mataram vassal to 1663/64) and Cliopatria's own Jambi row covers them from 1670; (3) the 1820 split of Riau-Lingga is four years before the 1824 treaty; (4) the Pahang separation is drawn in 1853, the Johor page dates the treaty 1861; (5) Terengganu leaves in 1727 in Cliopatria, 1722 on the page. The Sultanate of Malacca row (1459-1861) overlaps these years and is for the se-02 Malacca dossier.
PAGE SILENT: the end of the row in 1884 (dissolve at confidence 1; the British Colonial Empire 1885 shape contains all 61 cells of the last Johor shape); the 1726 Bugis/Minangkabau period; 1784 Dutch siege of Riau and 1818 Dutch Riau (the Johor page does not mention them); Abu Bakar and the 1885 treaty; Indragiri; Siak's separation after 1722 (the Siak Sultanate has no Cliopatria row); when the Sumatran shore (Riau, 287 cells) left Johor, which Cliopatria ties to 1820 and the page to 1824; the 3 north-Sumatra cells lost in 1626.
NEEDS DOSSIERS: Pahang Sultanate 1470-1623 (no Cliopatria row; pahang-sultanate is 1853-1889), Siak Sultanate (Raja Kecil, founded by 1722), the Jambi Kingdom before 1670.
Gazetteer: Pekan Tua, Sayong Pinang, Johor Lama, Bukit Seluyut, Batu Sawar, Kota Tinggi, Pancur, Lingga, Tungkal are not in the gazetteer; the coordinates are approximate and radii are used.
